As a child, I had always loved the gazebo. It was a sanctuary, a place to rest and reflect, and a reminder of simpler times. But as I stepped closer, I noticed something that made me pause.

The gazebo had always been surrounded by a lush carpet of green grass, but now, in its place, was a patch of withered brown blades. It was as if the grass had been struck by some unseen force and had been left to wither and die.
